title: Learn TypeScript from the ground up
hook: TypeScript adds static types to JavaScript without changing how code runs. This track starts with plain English, then grows into generics, narrowing, conditional types, and the depth you need for senior interviews and production APIs.

blocks.text: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript. You write .ts files. The TypeScript compiler (tsc) checks types, then emits plain JavaScript. Types are erased at run time — the engine still runs JavaScript. TypeScript adds interfaces, generics, narrowing, and utility types that C# developers will recognize, but assignability is structural, not nominal.

entries.plainDefinition: The tool that type-checks .ts files and emits JavaScript. Types disappear after compile.
entries.example: npm run build runs tsc before bundling.

entries.plainDefinition: TypeScript checks shape compatibility, not declaration names. If it looks like a duck, it is a duck.
entries.example: An interface is satisfied by any object with matching properties.

entries.plainDefinition: Compiler flag that treats null and undefined as distinct types requiring explicit handling.
entries.example: string is not assignable from null without a union or guard.

sections.heading: How it differs from C# and JavaScript

blocks.text: If you know C# or JavaScript, TypeScript borrows syntax from both. Like C#, you get interfaces and generics — but types erase at run time like JS, not IL metadata. Like JS, assignability is structural. strictNullChecks feels like C# nullable reference types, but enforcement is compile-time only.

rows: C#: metadata in IL; JS: none
C# NRT: compile + some run-time checks

blocks.text: Modules are numbered in learning order. Work through them in sequence unless a time map below fits your schedule. Each module ends with a mind map, a one-screen quick overview, and an interview page. This track has 18 modules and 101 topics.

items.title: Foundations (modules 01–07)
items.body: What TS is, basic types, type system, functions, classes, errors, and null safety. Finish before generics or conditional types.

items.title: Intermediate (modules 08–13)
items.body: Collections, generics, utility types, narrowing, conditional/mapped types, and async typing.

items.title: Advanced (modules 14–18)
items.body: Module resolution, advanced patterns, decorators, compiler tooling, and TS recap with interview radar.

items.title: Revise with mind maps and interview pages
items.body: Use mind maps and interview sections to reinforce what you learned — not as a shortcut around the topic pages.

items.title: Senior / FAANG depth layer (5+ years)
items.body: On intermediate and advanced topics (08–18), read Senior interview depth sections. Priority: infer-keyword, discriminated-unions-narrowing, conditional-types-basics, branded-and-opaque-types, strict-null-checks.

blocks.title: 101 topics — beginner clarity plus senior depth
blocks.body: Every topic keeps plain-English hooks and glossaries. Intermediate and advanced modules add runtime internals, tradeoffs, and FAANG-style interview scripts without removing the beginner layer.

stages.title: Foundations (01–07)
stages.summary: Static typing on top of JavaScript, compile pipeline, tsconfig, erasable types, and how TypeScript differs from C# on the CLR.

stages.title: Intermediate (08–13)
stages.summary: Typed arrays, Map/Set generics, tuple types, readonly tuples, satisfies operator, and collection typing patterns.

stages.title: Advanced (14–18)
stages.summary: moduleResolution, paths, ambient declarations, .d.ts files, declare module, triple-slash directives, and typing JS libraries.
